commands.review_summary:
The PR adds hard deadlines and stale-write guards to runtime authentication refresh, cold-start authentication preparation, and held-lock OAuth refresh paths, with regression tests.

PR surface: Source +167, Tests +372. Total +539 across 8 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current main has an unbounded shared runtime-auth refresh wait, and the contributor's real-timer evidence shows the new deadline releasing the handle, retrying, and discarding a stale completion.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] The remaining blocker is a narrow timeout-constant and invariant-test repair on the PR branch.

target.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock
target.body:
## Summary

A long-running gateway can permanently deadlock its entire agent lane on a stuck OAuth auth-refresh. The runtime auth single-flight in `auth-controller.ts` stores the in-flight refresh promise in `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight`; every model turn that needs auth does `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` **with no timeout**. If the underlying provider auth hook (`prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` -> OAuth refresh, keychain read, or cross-agent file-lock wait) never settles, `refreshInFlight` is never cleared and **every subsequent turn hangs forever** awaiting it. The process stays alive and the port stays open, so it looks healthy while no replies are produced.

Observed in production: a gateway froze mid-day right after a token hit expiry. Process alive (11d uptime, port listening) but fully idle since the freeze, zero sockets to the provider, all threads parked, one never-resolving `await`. On-disk token was valid the whole time (a fresh process pre-warmed auth in ~0.7s), and no on-disk lock was held — i.e. a pure in-memory single-flight deadlock.

This adds a hard deadline so the single-flight promise **always** settles:

- New `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline()` + `RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` (360s) in `runtime-auth-refresh.ts`. The worst legitimate case is two serialized in-lock budgets — waiting out a peer's full 150s critical section, then running our own 150s section — so 360s keeps 60s of real headroom above 300s; legitimate contention never misreports as a hard timeout while a true hang is forced to reject.
- `refreshRuntimeAuth` wraps the refresh operation in that deadline; on timeout it rejects, the `.finally` clears `refreshInFlight`, and all waiters unblock with a descriptive error instead of hanging.
- The `.finally` clear is no longer gated on `generation`: a profile rotation during a slow/hung refresh must still release the handle it owns, otherwise a stale handle wedges the new generation. The existing `refreshInFlight === refreshPromise` identity guard still prevents clobbering a newer refresh.

No behavior change on the happy path (fast refresh resolves long before the deadline). The deadline is a backstop only.

## Repro / Test plan

- [x] `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline` unit tests: rejects with the typed `RuntimeAuthDeadlineError` after the deadline when work never settles (fake timers), resolves/propagates when work wins the race, passes through unbounded for non-positive timeout, and the default exceeds two serialized in-lock budgets with explicit headroom.
- [x] `auth-controller` regression tests: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever sets `refreshInFlight`, then after advancing past the hard deadline the wedged handle rejects with `exceeded hard deadline` and is no longer the active in-flight handle; a deadline-abandoned refresh whose continuation later settles is discarded after a successful retry.
- [x] Proof the test catches the bug: with the deadline neutralized (timeout `0` = unbounded), the regression test **times out / FAILS**; restored, it passes.
- [x] Live repro harness (real timers, real 360s constant): deadline fires, lane recovers, stale completion discarded — full terminal capture in Evidence below.
- [x] Current-head scoped run: see Evidence below.

Thanks @amittell.

---

## Update: complete the deadlock class (not just the refresh path)

A follow-up audit found the original commit only backstopped ONE of several entry paths into the same auth lock/gate machinery. Both remaining paths could still permanently wedge the agent lane the same way:

1. **Cold-start / profile-rotation path (critical).** `applyApiKeyInfo` (the path `initializeAuthProfile` and `advanceAuthProfile` use, and the first turn a watchdog restart lands on) awaited `resolveApiKeyForCandidate` and `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` — the exact hook that hung in production — with no deadline. A single shared local `withAuthDeadline` helper now wraps every auth boundary in `auth-controller.ts` (refresh AND cold-start), so a hung provider hook fails the turn over instead of deadlocking the lane.
2. **In-lock keychain / buildApiKey (high).** In `oauth-manager.ts`, `withRefreshCallTimeout` wrapped only the network refresh call; the in-lock keychain store load and `buildApiKey` ran un-deadlined while the cross-agent file lock was held, so a wedged keychain pinned the lock and chain-stalled every same-key refresher behind the un-timed `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh gate (`refreshQueue.enqueue` chains each caller on the previous tail with no timeout). The whole held-lock critical section is now bounded by `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (150s), kept strictly between the 120s call timeout and the 180s stale window.

---

## Update 2: side-effect-safe timeouts (review findings)

The deadlines above abandon work they cannot cancel. The review correctly flagged that an abandoned continuation could later perform side effects while a successor owns the key. Head `08da7ebecf` closes both stale write-back paths and the budget arithmetic:

1. **In-lock OAuth write-back guard (`oauth-manager.ts`).** `withRefreshCallTimeout` now hands the critical section an ownership token (`{ state: "owned" | "abandoned" }`) that flips to `abandoned` the instant the section deadline fires — the same instant the file lock is released and a peer refresher can own the key. The continuation re-checks the token before **every** persist/mirror side effect (`adopt-bootstrap` write, refreshed-credential persist, main-store mirror) and no-ops with a debug log when stale, so it can never clobber a successor's freshly persisted tokens.
2. **Runtime auth generation invalidation (`auth-controller.ts` + `runtime-auth-refresh.ts`).** The deadline now rejects with a typed `RuntimeAuthDeadlineError`. When it abandons a refresh, the controller bumps `runtimeAuthState.generation`, so the abandoned completion — which snapshots generation/profile/source at entry — fails the existing stale-check and is discarded instead of overwriting the credentials a scheduled retry installed. Cold-start writes are sequenced strictly after their awaited deadline, so the abandoned cold-start work has no state write to guard beyond this.
3. **Outer budget headroom.** `RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` raised 300s -> 360s. The previous value equaled exactly two serialized 150s in-lock budgets with zero headroom, so worst-case legitimate contention could misreport as a hard timeout. The invariant test now asserts `> 2 x OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS + 30s` (strict, explicit margin) instead of the old `>=` sum.

Regression tests added for both guards: `oauth-manager.abandoned-writeback.test.ts` (real file locks and stores on disk; compressed budgets via the constants seam) and an `auth-controller` fake-timer test that proves a stale completion after deadline + retry cannot install its credentials.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Current `main` still awaits `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` in `auth-controller.ts` with no timeout, and the `.finally` clear is generation-gated, so one provider auth hook, keychain read, or cross-agent lock wait that never settles leaves the in-flight handle pending forever and every later model turn deadlocks awaiting it. The gateway process stays alive and its port stays open, so monitoring sees a healthy process while the agent lane produces no replies until a manual restart. This PR makes every runtime auth boundary settle — a hard 360s deadline on the single-flight refresh and cold-start paths, an ungated in-flight-handle clear, and a 150s bound on the whole held-lock OAuth critical section — and makes those deadlines side-effect-safe: abandoned continuations are ownership/generation-checked so they can never persist, mirror, or install credentials over a successor refresher.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` at d3ff48c51f. The only conflict this round was the import block of `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.ts` (main's #102009 egress-time credential injection vs this PR's deadline imports). Resolution keeps main's SecretRef egress guards exactly as shipped — `unwrapSecretSentinelsForProviderEgress` at the provider runtime-auth exchange, the `protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth` wrapper, and `secretSentinels: true` on `getApiKeyForModel` are byte-identical to `main` (the PR diff does not touch those lines) — and re-applies only the `withAuthDeadline` imports/wraps on top. The earlier `oauth-manager.ts` `KeyedAsyncQueue` resolution from the 22376d80e163 rebase is preserved unchanged.

Scoped test run at head 08da7ebecf5a83a0d7f8049643d38c775e7e1573:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts \
  src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts \
  src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.abandoned-writeback.test.ts

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  44 passed (44)
```

Sibling auth suites also pass at the same head (11 test files, 93 tests, 2 Vitest shards): `oauth-identity`, `oauth-lock-path`, `oauth-lock-timeout-classification`, `oauth-refresh-error`, `oauth-refresh-failure`, `oauth-refresh-queue`, `oauth-refresh-timeout`, `oauth-shared`, `oauth.adopt-identity`, `oauth.concurrent-agents`, `oauth.fallback-to-main-agent`, `oauth.mirror-refresh`, `oauth.openai-codex-refresh-fallback`, `oauth`, `effective-oauth`, `external-oauth`. `tsgo` core and core-test lanes exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on all changed files.

### Live repro 1 — runtime auth deadline, lane recovery, stale discard (real timers, real 360s constant)

One-shot harness wiring a never-resolving `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` into the real `createEmbeddedRunAuthController`; nothing mocked but the provider seam, no fake timers, unmodified production constants. Captured terminal output:

```
[t+0.0s] RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS = 360000ms
[t+0.0s] provider auth hook call 1: initial exchange succeeds (expires in 60s)
[t+0.0s] setRuntimeApiKey(custom-openai, initial-runtime-key)
[t+0.0s] initializeAuthProfile complete; scheduled refresh due in ~5s (min delay)
[t+5.0s] [controller debug] Refreshing runtime auth for custom-openai (scheduled)...
[t+5.0s] provider auth hook call 2: scheduled refresh HANGS (never settles) — the wedge
[t+5.0s] refreshInFlight handle set; awaiting the REAL 360s hard deadline...
[t+365.0s] [controller debug] Invalidated runtime auth generation 1 for custom-openai; deadline abandoned an in-flight refresh.
[t+365.0s] [controller warn] Runtime auth refresh failed for custom-openai: Runtime auth operation for custom-openai exceeded hard deadline (360000ms)
[t+365.0s] DEADLINE FIRED: refreshInFlight rejected with: Runtime auth operation for custom-openai exceeded hard deadline (360000ms)
[t+365.0s] single-flight handle cleared — the lane is no longer wedged
[t+365.0s] waiting for the 60s scheduled-retry to install fresh credentials...
[t+425.0s] [controller debug] Refreshing runtime auth for custom-openai (scheduled-retry)...
[t+425.0s] provider auth hook call 3: retry resolves fresh credentials
[t+425.0s] setRuntimeApiKey(custom-openai, retry-runtime-key)
[t+425.0s] [controller debug] Runtime auth refreshed for custom-openai; expires in 3600s.
[t+425.1s] LANE RECOVERED: retry installed retry-runtime-key (next turn can proceed)
[t+425.1s] resolving the abandoned call-2 hook with STALE credentials now
[t+425.1s] [controller debug] Ignoring stale runtime auth refresh for custom-openai; auth state advanced before scheduled refresh completed.
[t+426.1s] STALE COMPLETION DISCARDED: installed keys = [initial-runtime-key, retry-runtime-key] (no stale-runtime-key)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The deadline fires at the real 360s mark, the single-flight handle clears (lane un-wedged), the 60s scheduled retry installs fresh credentials (next turn proceeds), and the abandoned hook's eventual completion is discarded by the generation guard — `stale-runtime-key` is never installed.

### Live repro 2 — in-lock OAuth abandon, successor ownership, write-back discard (real file locks/stores)

Same-shape harness against the real `createOAuthManager` with the real cross-agent file lock and on-disk auth stores in a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; only the two deadline budgets are compressed (1s / 10s) via the constants seam so the run is observable. Captured terminal output:

```
[t+0.05s] seeded sub-agent store with expired credential (access=expired-access)
[t+0.05s] turn 1: resolveOAuthAccess enters the global refresh lock and wedges
[t+0.06s] refresh call 1: token endpoint HANGS (in-lock deadline will abandon it)
[t+1.07s] IN-LOCK DEADLINE FIRED: turn 1 rejected with: OAuth token refresh failed for openai: OAuth refresh call "openai oauth refresh critical section" exceeded hard timeout (1000ms)
[t+1.07s] turn 2 (lane recovery): a new refresher takes the lock and succeeds
[t+1.08s] refresh call 2: successor refresher rotates tokens successfully
[t+1.09s] [auth-profiles debug] mirrored refreshed OAuth credential to main agent store {"profileId":"openai:oauth","expires":"2026-07-09T01:37:34.322Z"}
[t+1.10s] LANE RECOVERED: turn 2 resolved apiKey=successor-access
[t+1.10s] abandoned call-1 continuation now settles with STALE rotated tokens
[t+1.10s] [auth-profiles debug] discarded abandoned OAuth refresh write-back after in-lock deadline {"profileId":"openai:oauth","provider":"openai","step":"persist"}
[t+1.60s] STALE WRITE-BACK DISCARDED: sub store access=successor-access, main mirror access=successor-access (stale-abandoned-access absent)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The `discarded abandoned OAuth refresh write-back after in-lock deadline` line is the FIX 1 guard firing; the on-disk stores (sub + main mirror) retain the successor's tokens and the abandoned refresher's rotated tokens are never persisted.

Production soak on a fork: gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run this patch backported on a fork since 2026-06, and the auth-refresh deadlock that previously froze the agent lane has not recurred.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: gateway agent lane permanently deadlocks when one runtime auth refresh never settles; every later model turn hangs on an un-timed `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` while the process looks healthy; additionally, deadline-abandoned refreshers could persist/mirror/install stale credentials over a successor refresher.
Real environment tested: live repro harnesses at head 08da7ebecf5a83a0d7f8049643d38c775e7e1573 run with real timers and the unmodified 360s production constant (runtime path) and real cross-agent file locks plus on-disk auth stores (OAuth path); production gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run the deadline patch backported on a fork since 2026-06 with no recurrence of the freeze.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.abandoned-writeback.test.ts
Evidence after fix: 4 test files, 44 tests passed at head 08da7ebecf5a83a0d7f8049643d38c775e7e1573; 11 sibling oauth suites (93 tests) green at the same head; captured live-harness terminal output above shows the 360s deadline firing by wall clock, the lane recovering on the next scheduled retry, and both stale write-backs being discarded with the guard log lines.
Observed result after fix: a hung provider auth hook or in-lock keychain wait now rejects at the deadline, the in-flight handle is cleared, waiting turns fail over with a descriptive error instead of deadlocking, abandoned continuations no-op instead of persisting or installing stale credentials, and the production fork gateways have had no recurrence of the freeze.
What was not tested: live upstream-main gateway soak at this exact head; full build and broad CI lanes are left to PR CI.
